function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Reykjavík – the clear winner** If you’re planning a trip to Iceland specifically because you love ice‑hockey—or just want to catch a game while exploring the country—*Reykjavík* will give you the richest experience. Here’s why: | What matters | Reykjavík | |--------------|-----------| | **Ice‑rinks & venues** | • *Laugardalshöll* – the biggest indoor arena in Iceland, home to the national team and the top‑tier league games.
• *Íshalinn* – a modern multi‑sport hall that regularly hosts club matches and youth tournaments.
*Other rinks*: several community rinks around the capital allow you to watch local leagues or even try skating yourself. | | **Team presence** | • **HC Þór** (formerly “Vikingur”) – one of the oldest clubs, playing at Laugardalshöll.
• National team practices often held here during international windows. | | **Accessibility** | • International airport right next door → easy arrival.
• Public transport links to all major sports complexes. | | **Accommodation & amenities** | • Wide range of hotels, hostels, Airbnbs—from luxury suites overlooking the harbor to budget-friendly rooms in the old town.
• Plenty of cafés, bars, and fine dining options nearby. | | **Sightseeing combo** | • While catching a match, you can stroll through Old Harbour, visit Harpa Concert Hall, explore the Sun Voyager sculpture, and enjoy whale‑watching cruises—all within walking distance. | --- ### Other notable spots | City | Why consider it? | |------|------------------| | **Akureyri** | Second‑largest city, known as the “Capital of North Iceland.” It houses *Akureyrarsvæðið* ice rink, which sees regular domestic league play. The surrounding fjords and hot springs make for great day trips after a game. | | **Kópavogur / Hafnarfjörður** | Close suburbs of Reykjavík with smaller rinks. Useful if you prefer quieter neighborhoods but still want quick access back to the capital’s larger venue. | | **Egilsstaðir** | Home to a modest rink that occasionally hosts regional competitions. Ideal for those who wish to see rural Icelandic life alongside their sport. | --- #### Quick travel tip Book your stay in Reykjavík early if you plan to attend a scheduled game—tickets sell out fast, especially during World Cup qualifiers or European Championship fixtures. Many hotels offer package deals that bundle accommodation + game tickets. --- **Bottom line:** For the full blend of competitive ice‑hockey action, convenience, and iconic Icelandic culture, head straight to Reykjavík. Its state‑of‑the‑art arenas, vibrant nightlife, and proximity to world‑class tourist sites make it the ultimate destination for both fans and casual visitors alike.
